stem: Lower-leaf chlorosis appears after a period of cool, saturated root-zone conditions. A feed record shows nitrogen was supplied within the approved program. Which conclusion is strongest?
choices: Nitrogen-related symptoms remain possible, but uptake limitation and root-zone conditions should be evaluated before concluding that the supply concentration itself is deficient.
The feed record proves nitrogen cannot be involved.
The symptom proves the fertilizer concentration must be increased.
Cool root-zone conditions can be ignored because only formulation determines nutrient status.
rationale: Nutrient symptoms can reflect supply, uptake, root function, environmental context, or interactions. A feed record does not by itself establish plant availability or cause.
